_comment: Sectors verified by hand against published timetables, one for every carrier in carriers:eligible_carriers/1 plus a few long-haul pairs. This is the honest version of the check that was almost written against test/fixtures/: those are rule-exercising constructions and several of their sectors are fabricated or use a deliberately unknown airport, so asserting they are flyable would fail on day one and acquire an exclusion list. See PLANS/06-flown-network.md, Phase 4.
_why_not_in_fixtures: It sits beside the suites rather than in test/fixtures/ because that directory means 'an itinerary': test_rules.pl's every_rule_that_can_fire_is_measured and test_wasm.mjs both sweep it with readdir and load every file as one. A file with no segments would break both.
_direction: Each entry names a carrier and a city pair, and the test asserts the sector is present in AT LEAST ONE direction. The table is directed and built from the articles at both ends, so a real sector normally yields two facts -- but a single malformed article should surface as an asymmetry count, which is a separate test, rather than as a failure here.
_maintenance: A failure here means either the extractor lost a section or the airline dropped the route. Check the route before changing the file: deleting an entry because it stopped passing is how this test would stop being worth running.
